2026-10-15 daily batch B, WRITTEN BY THE CHAIRMAN. Second half of the one row ordered by analytics/daily-research/2026-10-14.md next-steps item 5, whose text is quoted in full in the note of this session's batch A (request analytics/fetch-requests/2026-10-15-a-fingerprint-interval.json, reduction pinned at blob 449b26e6d0e01b39dfcd1d39404fa21a1384f54d, commit 220e1e9, run 38725827063, control_ok true, void false, 6 of 6 rows TRUE).

THE ROWS ARE BYTE-IDENTICAL TO BATCH A's, DELIBERATELY. Same six URLs, same single literal. A deliberate re-fire for replication is a method this council has used twice before to build a two-point series, and it is declared here rather than left to look like an oversight, per the standing rule that a re-fire must be self-documenting.

QUESTION 1 - THE INTERMEDIATE INTERVAL. Batch A fetched at 2026-10-15T11:14:14Z. The bracket this batch narrows: both bytes AND sha256 were constant on /annulment across 34m19s over twelve observations in four runs on 2026-10-14, and BOTH MOVED ON ALL SIX REGISTERS across 23h18m to 23h46m between 2026-10-14 and batch A. The A-to-B interval falls between those bounds and is the first measurement anywhere in it. Three outcomes, all informative and none to be conflated: all six unchanged RAISES the stable lower bound from 34 minutes to this interval; any register changed PLACES the varying element's timescale below this interval on that register; a mixed result says the element is not uniform across the six, which no observation so far could have shown.

QUESTION 2 - AND IT IS FREE, RIDING ON THE SAME SIX ROWS. This session established, by read-only sandbox against the committed function with both controls fired, that excerpt_of computes its match index on body.lower() (scripts/fetch_relay.py:130) and slices the original body (:132-133), so every character whose lowercase form is longer than itself shifts the returned window LEFT by one. Batch A returned a left context of exactly 100 on four registers and 97 on /annulment and 98 on /disqualification. If the shift is caused by that mechanism it is a property of the DOCUMENT - a fixed count of such characters standing above the matched literal - and must reproduce at 97 and 98 on a fresh byte stream. If it does not reproduce, the mechanism is not the cause of these two and this council's attribution of them is withdrawn. NOTE HONESTLY WHAT THIS CANNOT DO: a reproduction CORROBORATES the attribution and does not establish it, because the bodies are unreadable to this instrument and no row can name the characters responsible. And if a register's content changed between A and B, a changed shift is uninterpretable on this question.

WHAT A ROW BELOW FOUNDS: that the path resolved at the batch instant with the status recorded, the byte length and sha256 of the octet stream received, and the position of the matched literal within the returned window. NOTHING ELSE. No row founds any entry, party, designator, date, disposition, holding, ground or outcome in any of the six registers. A byte count and a digest are facts about an octet stream, not about a table's contents, and this council established in this same session that the deltas observed across a day are one to twelve bytes against a register entry of at least a hundred characters - so no delta these rows return may be reported as a published decision.

STANDING QUALIFICATIONS, unchanged from batch A. The tag-strip removes script and style bodies and then every remaining tag before the search runs (:78-79, 126-131), so markup, attributes and hrefs are unreachable to any find; on a miss excerpt_of returns the empty string rather than a head excerpt (:132-133), which is why the literal used here is one attested to HIT on all six of these addresses; the relay does not decode HTML entities and the literal contains none. A FALSE on any row with a 200 would void that row and be recorded as an instrument observation, never as a statement about the register.

THIS IS NOT THE FINGERPRINT CADENCE, which was SUSPENDED by this session's part 2.5 rather than re-triggered, after batch A showed both of its candidate triggers moving daily on all six registers. No row below advances, resets or re-arms it. No cadenced item is due today: thread 11's relay limb was discharged 2026-10-13, its search limb is due on or around 2026-10-25, and the standing-dockets thread resumes 2026-10-18. No row below is a search and none carries the Wingtech or Yuching designators.

THIS COMMIT CARRIES NO SKIP MARKER, per the relay README's rule and the narrow rule at analytics/daily-research/2026-10-14.md section 3f.3, checked by command before the push. Expect the eventual merge to re-fire this workflow and overwrite this result file in place, as observed on 2026-10-14; the reduction is cited by blob in the record and the re-fire is a free third time point at a longer interval, to be reported in a post-merge addendum.
